story: Gary is on Magnolia Loop, patiently explaining to Hal that the parade cart's wiring will be bench-tested in the garage until the committee signs off tomorrow, while Hal dutifully counts the pink flamingos visible from the street. Over at the Rec Center, Donna is determinedly reserving a court for a two-hour practice session with Gary, and across town Rosa is at the Town Hall review desk, filing the cart folder with Gary's clamp list and light layout. The humid Thursday haze hangs at 82 degrees as the whole community waits, a little impatiently, for the committee to weigh in.
events: Donna (court reservation kiosk): Reserve a court for a two-hour practice session with Gary
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street
Rosa (architectural review desk): Submit the parade cart folder with Gary's clamp list and light layout

gary.thought_process: Hal just asked whether the cart modifications go through Architectural Review. I already told him last tick that the application is filed, nothing's cleared, and the cart stays in the garage. He's now citing L-01 and mentioning the committee meets tomorrow, which is useful: the review is the path forward, and I don't want to repeat myself. I should acknowledge his point, confirm I'm following the rule, and note Rosa has the sketches headed to the desk. Then I can wrap up and get to wiring work in the garage. Keep it short and honest; no street modifications until approval.

parameters.content: That's exactly the route I'm taking, Hal. Good to know the committee sits tomorrow. Rosa's got my sketches and clamp list at the desk, and nothing goes on the cart where the street can see it until they sign off. I'll be in the garage bench-testing the wiring in the meantime.

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center with no one around, and I just studied the ladder standings last tick. Gary hasn't arrived yet, and I don't want to nag him again after already inviting him to practice. The court reservation kiosk is the productive move: I can book a court for our practice session, staying within the two-hour limit (L-05), so when Gary shows up we're ready to climb past Pruitt-Kowalski.

parameters.content: Reserve a court for a two-hour practice session with Gary

hal.thought_process: Gary just told me he's keeping the cart in the garage until the committee clears it, which is exactly what L-01 asks. That settles my complaint about the cart for now. Donna's flamingos are right here on the street, though, and L-02 caps visible ornaments at three. A by-the-book man counts before he reports, so I'll tally the flock myself and decide whether a straight word to Donna comes first. No point lingering on Gary; he's done right by me.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street

rosa.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall on Thursday afternoon with the Halloween parade Saturday. Gary's clamp list and light layout are in the folder, and the plan was to walk to the review desk with Donna. Nobody's here yet, but I'm the one carrying the folder, so I should get the paperwork moving. Filing the cart application at the architectural review desk is the honest, rules-following thing to do, and it describes exactly what we're building, tuck-on and temporary. Once it's filed, Donna and Gary can join me or follow up.

parameters.content: Submit the parade cart folder with Gary's clamp list and light layout

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
